current_inventory.description_angle: Playful Yinka Ilori color, unusual M.A.D.1S architecture, and a strong design-object presence with real mechanical interest.
talking_points: The Nature edition pairs a green rotor with purple and red straps, so it feels intentionally artistic rather than merely colorful.
The slimmer M.A.D.1S case keeps the eccentric display more wearable than earlier M.A.D.1 executions.
The rotating hours cylinder and central rotor make it conversational on the wrist even before anyone asks what it is.
This is a bold piece with very little visual anonymity, which is part of the appeal but also the main tradeoff.

current_inventory.description_angle: Stealthy ceramic, architectural skeleton dial, modern material-focused watch with strong visual presence.
talking_points: The matte black ceramic construction gives the watch a lightweight, modern, stealthy feel.
Rose gold-tone accents add warmth and contrast without making the watch feel overly flashy.
The skeleton dial and exhibition caseback make the movement a major visual part of the experience.
At 43mm with strong contrast, it has real wrist presence and may feel large for buyers who prefer compact watches.

current_inventory.bracelet: Black calf leather strap over red rubber with ceramic-coated buckle
current_inventory.set_contents: Watch, original Bell & Ross box, and Jomashop paperwork
current_inventory.condition: Excellent — personal piece, worn sparingly. Case and dial present essentially as new; the strap shows light wear consistent with careful use.
current_inventory.description_angle: Limited collaboration with Sacha Lakic's Blacktrack custom motorcycle studio. Smoked grey-on-black chronograph dial with red café racer accents and the Blacktrack bike engraved on the caseback. A numbered piece (131/500) that rarely comes up for sale, offered at $3,200 — well under launch pricing.
talking_points: Limited to 500 pieces worldwide and individually numbered — this example is 131/500, engraved on the caseback alongside the Blacktrack motorcycle.
Designed with Sacha Lakic, the designer behind Blacktrack's custom café racers, which is where the red-edged strap and motorsport dial accents come from.
The bi-material strap is black calf leather over red rubber, so the red only flashes at the edges in motion — subtle until it isn't.
Comes from Mir's personal collection with box and Jomashop paperwork, priced at $3,200.
